gaps.construct: with self._condition: (acquire a re-entrant lock for a block, release on every exit)
gaps.description: The doc rules out shared mutable state between tasks and says there is nothing for a lock to protect, so there is no lock type and no locked block; 'hold guard as locked condition of future' is invented by analogy with hold for files.

gaps.construct: self._condition.notify_all() waking threads blocked in result() or wait()
gaps.description: No condition variables, wait or notify; structured concurrency (together, pipeline) covers fork-join and queues but not one thread signalling others that are already blocked.

gaps.construct: the Future is mutated by the executor thread while client threads hold it; waiters are shared objects owned elsewhere
gaps.description: editable means exclusive ownership; there is no shared reference type, so 'editable shared' and 'List of shared Waiter' are invented.

gaps.construct: _invoke_callbacks runs user-registered done callbacks after the lock is released
gaps.description: No type for a stored operation, and no way to state in a header the effects of callbacks supplied by others; 'uses callbacks' is a placeholder.
Future of T is declared, but the doc has no way for an operation to introduce T.

gaps.construct: set_result is a method; Executor subclasses and tests call it on a shared instance
gaps.description: No methods or self; written as 'set_result result on future'.
Failures in the doc are bare names with no payload or message, and there is no repr; the diagnostic text is lost.

gaps.construct: self._state in {CANCELLED, CANCELLED_AND_NOTIFIED, FINISHED} (set literal membership)
gaps.description: Only list literals exist; a list of variants is used with 'is in', which works but whether 'is in' applies to variants of a choice is not stated.

gaps.construct: uses line for an operation whose effects are on shared memory and other threads
gaps.description: The doc's uses lists capabilities; whether a lock, a condition, or a shared object counts as a capability is not settled.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one.
A task cannot outlive its scope (the Future is set by a worker thread long after the submitting scope continues)
invented_syntax: hold guard as locked condition of future
uses condition of future (a field as a capability)
uses callbacks (a capability name for unknown stored-callback effects)
notes: Scribe's structured-concurrency model is a deliberate restriction, and this function belongs to the layer that implements futures beneath it; it cannot be written without shared mutable state, a lock and a condition variable. The designer should decide whether such runtime primitives are a declared non-goal provided by a trusted foreign library (with 'trust'), or whether Scribe needs a lower, unsafe tier for them. If the former, the doc should say so and show the boundary.
